BBC News (David Cowan, Scotland home affairs correspondent) — published Thursday 24 September 2026 06:14 BST (05:14 UTC)
SECOND SOURCE: Sky News, "'Powerful organised crime group' targeted as hundreds of officers carry out raids", https://news.sky.com/video/sky-news-joins-police-on-scotlands-largest-ever-human-trafficking-raid-13591362 (filed ~12:15 BST)

HEADLINE: Police Scotland's largest ever human trafficking operation — 36 arrests, 14 cannabis farms found, 47 addresses searched.

FACTS (BBC):
- About 300 officers took part in simultaneous early-morning raids on Wednesday 23 September; 36 arrests; 14 cannabis-growing operations discovered.
- 47 addresses searched or checked in Aberdeen, Dundee, Falkirk, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Ayrshire, Lanarkshire, Midlothian and the Scottish Borders. Arrests were also made in Birmingham.
- Police Scotland allege the group is involved in "poly-criminality": human trafficking, drug production, fraud, money laundering and organised immigration crime.
- The investigation began after Vietnamese criminals were connected to 150 cannabis farms found in Scotland last year; around 120 people were arrested as "gardeners" and £26m of drugs seized. A single crime group was later linked to about a third of the farms.
- Operation carried out with Home Office Immigration Enforcement and HMRC. National Crime Agency officers based in Hanoi have been liaising with Vietnamese authorities.
- Sites included a tenement flat in Edinburgh's South Clerk Street, five minutes from a busy police station, and a nail salon in Glasgow.
- Police will now establish whether any of those arrested are themselves trafficking victims.

QUOTES:
Det Supt Stevie Bertram, Police Scotland (BBC): "This was by far the biggest human trafficking investigation that Police Scotland has ever run." / "We wanted to disrupt and absolutely cripple that organisation. We wanted to do it all in one day and I think it's been a huge success. Essentially, they won't be able to function." / "All of the targets of this operation have been arrested and they are the ones we believe are running that operation." / "We think the group runs across the UK and internationally." / "Vietnamese nationals are still the highest nationality that we see being exploited in Scotland."
